title: How to find UK jobs with visa sponsorship after studying
summary: Use the sponsor register to shortlist employers, check actual vacancies and get a role-specific answer before relying on a job for your next visa.
content:
# How to find UK jobs with visa sponsorship after studying

Last updated: 2026-11-26

## Start with the vacancy
Search for roles that fit your skills and that say sponsorship is available for this vacancy. Use employer careers pages, your university careers service, the public Find a Job service where relevant and graduate job boards. Use a job board as a lead and check the employer's own advert. Record the vacancy ID, closing date, start date, employer name and exact sponsorship wording. A company with a licence can still rule out sponsorship for certain teams, sites or graduate schemes. [Where to search](#guide-evidence-start)

## Verify the legal employer
Open the Home Office register of licensed worker sponsors and download the current list. Search the legal name, an alternate spelling if needed, and the town. Check the route column for Skilled Worker as well as the rating. Ask HR which legal entity would employ and sponsor you if the advert uses a brand name. A different subsidiary or an agency may not be covered by the licence you found. Record the date you checked and confirm again before relying on any offer. [Sponsor register](#guide-evidence-register) · [How employer sponsorship works](/en/work-visa/skilled-worker-sponsorship-cos)

## Run two searches in parallel
Many larger structured schemes open in autumn for the following year's start. Some assess applications as they arrive or close early. Keep a second list of rolling or immediate-start jobs and check actual dates. In technology and engineering compare the duties, tools and required experience. In finance or creative roles, check the exact stream and its contract. Health roles may require professional registration, and adult social care has distinct sponsorship rules. The institution or subject you studied does not determine whether an offer meets immigration rules. [Recruitment cycles](#guide-evidence-cycles)

## Ask HR before you commit
Tell the employer which permission you have and when it expires. Answer current right-to-work and future sponsorship questions separately and accurately. Ask: “Can your employing entity sponsor this vacancy under Skilled Worker? If yes, when can HR confirm the CoS, occupation code, contracted hours and basic salary?” A Graduate holder who can start today may still need sponsorship to finish the contract. For example, if a scheme starts after your permission expires and the recruiter answers only that the firm has a licence, ask for a role-specific written answer and keep applying while you wait. [Work permission and switching](#guide-evidence-ask) · [Check a Skilled Worker offer](/en/work-visa/check-skilled-worker-job-offer)

## Work back from expiry
Compare the eVisa or latest UKVI notice with the scheme deadline, offer, start date and expected CoS date. If a sponsor and qualifying job are ready in time, check whether you can switch directly from Student permission. If you need time to look and qualify for Graduate permission, weigh its cost and expiry. Before a Graduate visa expires, identify any route you genuinely qualify for and allow enough time for a valid application. A job offer, application interview or promise of a future CoS does not extend your permission. Get regulated advice if you are close to expiry and plan to leave in time if there is no lawful basis to stay. [Switch or get advice](#guide-evidence-deadline) · [Graduate visa timing](/en/work-visa/graduate-visa-uk) · [Options after study](/en/work-visa/uk-options-after-graduation)
